subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding muscles in general?

options.label: a
options.text: Origin of muscle moves during contraction

options.label: b
options.text: Insertion of muscle is fixed during contraction

options.label: c
options.text: Origin and insertion of muscle is fixed during contraction

options.label: d
options.text: Origin of muscle is fixed during contraction

correct_answer_text: Origin of muscle is fixed during contraction

explanation.text:
The origin of the muscle is fixed, while the insertion moves during contraction.

Skeletal muscles exert their force on bones through tendon attachments; the generated force helps produce movement or maintain posture.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following is a true statement regarding skeletal muscle?

options.label: a
options.text: Muscle groups are surrounded by endomysium

options.label: b
options.text: Muscle fibers are surrounded by endomysium

options.label: c
options.text: Muscle groups are surrounded by perimysium

options.label: d
options.text: Muscle fibers are surrounded by perimysium

correct_answer_text: Muscle fibers are surrounded by endomysium

explanation.text:
Muscle fibres are surrounded by a delicate connective-tissue network called endomysium.

Endomysium surrounds individual muscle fibers; perimysium surrounds bundles of muscle fibers (fasciculi); epimysium surrounds the whole muscle or muscle groups.

The endomysial, perimysial and epimysial layers fuse where muscles connect to adjacent structures such as tendons, aponeuroses and fasciae.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following muscles does not predominantly contain oblique fasciculi?

explanation.text:
Rectus abdominis contains parallel fasciculi; the other listed muscles have oblique fasciculi.

Muscle fasciculi may be parallel to the line of pull, oblique to it, or arranged in a spiral/twisted pattern.

Parallel muscles can be quadrilateral, strap-like, strap-like with tendinous intersections, or fusiform.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following accurately describes the shape of trapezius muscle?

explanation.text:
Trapezius individually is a flat, triangular muscle extending over the back of the neck and upper thorax. Paired trapezius muscles resemble a trapezium, which gives the muscle its name.

Oblique-fiber muscles include triangular and pennate patterns. Pennate subtypes include unipennate, bipennate, multipennate and circumpennate (radial).

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Identify the type of muscle marked as X in the image below.

explanation.text:
The muscle marked X is pectoralis major, a spiral muscle.

Spiral muscles have a twisted arrangement; pectoralis major sternocostal fibers and latissimus dorsi undergo about a 180° twist between attachments, while supinator winds obliquely around the proximal radius.

Cruciate is a spiral subtype in which two or more muscle-fiber planes run in differing directions; sternocleidomastoid, masseter and adductor magnus are examples described by the source.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following muscles do not have parallel oriented muscle fibers?

explanation.text:
Tibialis anterior has oblique muscle fibers arranged in a circumpennate (radial) fashion rather than parallel fibers. Fibers arise from the walls of its osteofascial compartment and converge obliquely on a central tendon.

Sartorius, rectus abdominis and sternohyoid have parallel fibers.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: A 40-year-old man with chronic liver disease presented with complaints of inability to straighten his ring finger completely as shown in the image. The broad sheet-like tendon involved in this condition is the ______

explanation.text:
The condition is Dupuytren's contracture, involving contracture of the flat broad sheet-like tendon called an aponeurosis and producing flexion deformity, especially of the ring and little fingers.

An aponeurosis is a pearly-white sheet of fibrous tissue replacing tendons in sheet-like muscles with broad attachment. It resembles tendon histologically and is sparsely supplied by blood vessels and nerves.

Examples include palmar and plantar aponeuroses, anterior abdominal aponeuroses, anterior/posterior intercostal membranes and the scalp galea aponeurotica.

A retinaculum is a strong short broad fibrous band retaining tendons; a raphe is a linear fibrous band formed by interdigitation of tendinous/aponeurotic ends; fascia is a generic term for visible connective-tissue sheaths or sheets.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following statements regarding myofibrils is false?

options.label: a
options.text: The A band consists of both thick and thin filaments

options.label: b
options.text: The I band consists of only thin filaments

options.label: c
options.text: The H zone consists of only thick filaments

options.label: d
options.text: Z disc is present in the middle of A band

correct_answer_text: Z disc is present in the middle of A band

explanation.text:
The Z disc (Krause membrane) lies in the middle of the I band, not the A band.

The A band contains both thick and thin filaments; the H band within it contains only thick filaments and the M line lies centrally. The I band contains only thin filaments and has the Z disc centrally.

The segment of a myofibril between two Z discs is the sarcomere.

The A band contains both thick and thin filaments; the H band within it contains only thick filaments and the M line lies centrally. The I band contains only thin filaments and has the Z disc centrally.
The segment of a myofibril between two Z discs is the sarcomere.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Identify the true statement about the motor nerve supply of the muscle.

options.label: a
options.text: α-efferents are small unmyelinated nerve fibers

options.label: b
options.text: Autonomic efferents supply vascular smooth muscles

options.label: d
options.text: α-efferents supply the intrafusal muscle fibers

correct_answer_text: Autonomic efferents supply vascular smooth muscles

explanation.text:
Autonomic efferents supply vascular smooth muscle fibers.

Every skeletal muscle is supplied by a mixed motor nerve containing motor and sensory fibers. Extrafusal muscle fibers receive large myelinated α-efferents; intrafusal spindle fibers receive small myelinated γ-efferents; vascular smooth muscle receives fine unmyelinated autonomic efferents.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: The ‘flower spray endings’ present in the muscle spindle are __________

explanation.text:
Flower spray endings in muscle spindles are secondary sensory nerve endings.

Muscle spindles receive thickly myelinated Ia and thinly myelinated II afferents. Primary Ia annulospiral endings lie in the central nuclear region, while secondary II flower-spray endings lie on either side of the nuclei.

The Golgi tendon organ is supplied by large myelinated Ib afferents. Connective-tissue sheaths receive fine myelinated and unmyelinated axons carrying pain and other sensations.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: How many muscle fibers do a small motor unit consist of?

explanation.text:
A small motor unit has 5-10 muscle fibers.

A motor unit (myone) is one α motor neuron together with all muscle fibers it supplies. Fine-control muscles have fewer fibers per neuron; gross-movement muscles may have many.

The source describes small motor units (5-10 fibers) in fine-movement muscles such as extraocular muscles, and large motor units (100-2000 fibers) in gross-movement muscles such as proximal limb muscles.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: Which of the following is not a hybrid muscle?

explanation.text:
Flexor carpi ulnaris is not a hybrid muscle because it is supplied by a single nerve (ulnar nerve).

A composite/hybrid muscle is supplied by two different nerves with different root values and usually has different sets of fibers with separate nerve supplies.

Examples listed include brachialis, pectoralis major, iliopsoas, subscapularis, biceps femoris, adductor magnus, digastric, flexor pollicis brevis, flexor digitorum profundus, pectineus, opponens pollicis and trapezius.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: What type of muscle fibers do the postural muscles predominantly contain?

options.label: d
options.text: Both type I and II fibers

explanation.text:
Postural muscles predominantly contain Type I (slow-twitch) fibers, which show slow tonic contraction.

Muscle fibers are broadly Type I (slow contracting/slow-twitch) and Type II (fast contracting/fast-twitch); Type II is further divided into IIA and IIX/IIB.

subject: Anatomy
question_text: You notice a lady performing the following exercise to strengthen her abdominal muscles at the gym. It involved maintaining the muscle contraction without a change in muscle length, by not moving any of her joints. It is a type of ______

explanation.text:
Contraction without a change in muscle length is isometric contraction; a plank is an isometric exercise.

Isotonic contraction maintains constant tension while muscle length changes and may be concentric or eccentric. Concentric contraction shortens muscle, whereas eccentric contraction lengthens it.

Isometric contraction generates force while maintaining constant muscle length; examples include holding a crouched position or a wall-sit.
